clue.text: Gurgling of infant almost blew wife away

indicators.note: something almost complete stops just short, so the final letter of the word before is dropped
sending something away removes it, so the named letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: an infant is a baby; its last letter goes
taken as written
W is the standard abbreviation for wife; it is removed from the word before

explanation.surface: A baby's burble so forceful it nearly blew a wife off her feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gurgling of infant' reads as one phrase, but only 'Gurgling' defines; 'infant almost' is BAB(y) and 'blew wife away' is BLEW losing its W.
explanation.definitionFit: Babbling is the meaningless burbling sound of a baby or a stream, close enough to gurgling to stand as a synonym.

clue.text: Snub bishop and scarper

parts.note: B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop
to scarper is to run away quickly, to rush off

explanation.surface: A churchman, slighted, takes to his heels.
explanation.walkthrough: Scarper is British slang for running away.
explanation.definitionFit: A brush-off is a curt rejection or dismissal, which is exactly what a snub amounts to.

clue.text: Uncouth behaviour of yobbo near Barking

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, and mad letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lout's loutishness on show close to Barking, a district of east London.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking looks like the London place-name, but as 'barking mad' it signals the jumble. A yobbo is a British lout.
explanation.definitionFit: Baboonery is behaviour likened to a baboon's, coarse and boorish, a direct match for uncouth conduct.

clue.text: Business alliance oddly failing

indicators.note: the letters in odd positions fail to appear, leaving only every second one

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters are kept

explanation.surface: A corporate partnership collapsing in strange fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Business alliance' looks like one thing; the first word is the definition and 'alliance' the source of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: One's line is one's trade or field of work, as in 'what line are you in?', a sense of business.

clue.text: Junior doctor is humane, so struggling

indicators.note: something struggling is in disarray, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A kind-hearted trainee medic finds the job hard going.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals a houseman was a newly qualified doctor in a first hospital post, a junior doctor.

clue.text: Earthy, rousing chorus about hero's end

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged word goes around the other piece
rousing stirs things up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: 'end' keeps only the last letter of 'hero'

parts.note: the last letter of hero

explanation.surface: A full-throated, rousing chorus sung around a hero's death.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled chorus wraps around the final letter of hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochrous means of or like ochre, an earthy clay pigment, so it describes an earthy colour or substance.

clue.text: Perhaps watch person of little importance

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: a little timepiece, of which a watch is one example

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is whimsical: a watch is perhaps a little timer, split as two words. 'Perhaps' flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: A small-timer is someone operating on a minor scale, a nobody, while a wristwatch is literally a small device for timing.

clue.text: Elk sounds like a cow on Ecstasy

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another sits above it, so the first comes before the second

parts.note: a cow moos; 'sounds like a cow' is the verb, not a sound-alike signal
E is slang for the drug Ecstasy

explanation.surface: An elk makes a noise like a cow that has taken drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds like' looks like a homophone signal, but here it simply means 'makes the noise of'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Europe the elk is the same animal North Americans call the moose, the largest deer.

clue.text: Nakedness of some chums I'd unfortunately seen from below

indicators.note: in a down entry, viewing from the bottom up means reading the letters upward, end to start
some means only part, so a run of letters is taken from inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of chums, all of I'd and the start of unfortunately

explanation.surface: Mates regrettably glimpsed undressed from a low vantage point.
explanation.definitionFit: Nudism is the practice of going without clothes, a state of nakedness.

clue.text: Hybrid beast with nervy twitches

parts.note: W is a standard abbreviation for with

indicators.note: twitches are jerky spasms, so the letters jerk out of their order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A cross-bred monster with anxious tics.
explanation.definitionFit: A wyvern is a heraldic creature, part dragon and part serpent, with two legs and a barbed tail: a composite monster.

clue.text: Apocryphal story of man hurt by bats

indicators.note: bats is slang for crazy, so the letters go crazy and change places

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tall tale about someone injured by flying bats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bats' reads as the flying mammals, which fits the tall-tale surface, but it is the adjective meaning mad.
explanation.definitionFit: An urban myth is a widely repeated modern tale that is untrue, which is what apocryphal means.

clue.text: Egg protected by devoted duck

indicators.note: something protected is held safely inside its guardian, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: avid means keen, devoted
an egg is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: An egg kept safe by a doting duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like the bird sitting on the egg, but it is the verb meaning dodge.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck a question or a blow is to dodge it, and so to avoid it.

clue.text: Ghetto gangster

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for a run-down inner-city neighbourhood
second meaning: slang for a thug or hoodlum

explanation.surface: A street criminal from the poor quarter.
explanation.definitionFit: The 'hood is slang short for neighbourhood, especially a deprived one, and a hood is short for hoodlum, a gangster.

clue.text: Unable to kick Oscar badly in alcove

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the first pieces sit within the last

parts.note: a recess is an alcove set back in a wall
Oscar is the NATO alphabet word for O
ill means badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: Someone is too feeble to kick Oscar, perhaps a dog, sulking in a nook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kick' is not a footballer's kick but the backward jolt of a fired gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A recoilless gun is designed not to jolt back when fired, so it is unable to kick.

clue.text: Time to support teams on plane, perhaps in minor way

indicators.note: in a down clue a support goes underneath, so this piece comes after the others

parts.note: sides are teams in a match
the plane is a kind of tree; 'perhaps' marks an example
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Teams travelling on an aircraft need time to back each other in some small way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plane' suggests an aircraft carrying teams; it is the plane tree, common in London streets. 'On' places one piece above the next.
explanation.definitionFit: A side street is a minor road branching off a main one, a lesser way.

clue.text: Give female dictionary missing the letter C

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the named letter is absent from the word

parts.note: a lexicon is a dictionary
taken as written; this letter is removed

explanation.surface: An instruction to hand a woman a dictionary with C omitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give' looks like a verb opening an instruction, but it is the noun meaning capacity to bend.
explanation.definitionFit: Flexion is bending, and give as a noun is the yielding or bending of a material under pressure.

clue.text: Vacuous Scotsman with long nose

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the word is emptied of its insides and only its ends remain

parts.note: the first and last letters
to long for something is to itch for it

explanation.surface: An empty-headed Scot with a big nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long nose' reads as one feature; 'long' is the verb yearn and 'nose' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A nose is slang for a police informer, someone who sniffs out and reports others, which is what a snitch is.

clue.text: Bubbly chap suffering with mange

indicators.note: suffering things are in a bad state, so the letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheerful man is afflicted with a skin disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bubbly' looks like an adjective for the chap, but it is the noun for fizzy wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Bubbly is informal for sparkling wine, and champagne is the classic example.

clue.text: Caught one extremely gutless, thievish canine

indicators.note: to catch a remark is to hear it, so what follows is taken by its sound

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I, which is said like the organ of sight
too means excessively, extremely

indicators.note: gutted of its insides, the word keeps only its outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A thieving coward was nabbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' sounds like an arrest, but it means heard; 'extremely' looks like a letter-selection signal attached to gutless, yet it simply gives a word meaning 'excessively'.
explanation.definitionFit: The eye tooth is the canine tooth of the upper jaw, so named for sitting below the eye.

clue.text: Extremely hairy ape repelled an aardwolf, perhaps

indicators.note: at the extremes means at the ends, so only first and last letters of each word are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters
the first and last letters

indicators.note: something repelled is driven back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written, then turned around

explanation.surface: A shaggy ape fended off a termite-eating relative of the hyena.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks the aardwolf as an example: it is an African member of the hyena family that feeds on termites.
explanation.definitionFit: The aardwolf belongs to the hyena family, so it is a kind of hyaena, the older spelling.

clue.text: Originally adored revolutionary communist students to bits

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so only the first letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter

indicators.note: a revolution turns things right round, so the following words are read backwards

parts.note: red is a common term for a communist
the NUS is Britain's National Union of Students

explanation.surface: Beloved radical leftist students torn apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary communist' reads as a political description, but 'revolutionary' turns round both the communist and the students.
explanation.definitionFit: Asunder means into separate pieces, as in torn asunder, i.e. to bits.

clue.text: People embracing music as method of healing

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug and enclose, so one word wraps around another

parts.note: they means people in general
rap is a genre of music

explanation.surface: Crowds turn to music for healing.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapy is treatment intended to heal or relieve a disorder, a way of making someone well.

clue.text: Top 30 for the most part contains the ultimate in dross

indicators.note: contains means holds inside, so the shortened word wraps around the extra letter
most but not all means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the number written as a word, then cut short

indicators.note: 'the ultimate in' keeps only the last letter of 'dross'

parts.note: the last letter of dross

explanation.surface: A chart-topping Top 30 that is mostly rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top 30' reads as a music chart; 'Top' alone is the definition, a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A top is a garment for the upper body, and a T-shirt is a common kind of top.

clue.text: American's exclamation as Finn briefly boards ship

indicators.note: to board a vessel is to get inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: SS is the prefix for steamship

indicators.note: briefly means in short form, so a word is cut down

parts.note: Huckleberry Finn is Mark Twain's boy hero, here shortened to his nickname

explanation.surface: An American cries out as a Finn hops briefly aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finn' looks like a man from Finland, but it is Huck Finn, whose first name is cut to its usual short form.
explanation.definitionFit: Shucks is a mild American interjection of embarrassment or disappointment.

clue.text: Unwelcome words hurt them so badly

indicators.note: done badly, the letters end up in a wrong, jumbled order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Harsh remarks wounded some people deeply.
explanation.definitionFit: Home truths are unpleasant facts about oneself that one would rather not hear, so they are unwelcome words.

clue.text: Setter's sandwiches on last of rye bread

indicators.note: a sandwich holds its filling between two slices, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me
taken as written

indicators.note: the last of something is its final part, so only the end letter is used

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler making sandwiches with rye bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rye bread' reads as one loaf; 'bread' is the definition, slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is long-standing slang for money, as in earning one's bread.

clue.text: Barney expectorated

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a petty quarrel; barney is British slang for a row
second meaning: past tense of the verb meaning to eject saliva

explanation.walkthrough: Barney looks like a name, but in British slang a barney is a noisy argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A spat is a short petty quarrel, and spat is also the past tense of spit, to expectorate.

clue.text: Smell fine bit of fish on the turn

indicators.note: turning round sends things back the way they came, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
a fin is a part of a fish

explanation.surface: Some fish that is going off gives off a nice odour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the turn' suits fish going bad; here it turns the letters round. Niff is British slang for a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Niff is informal British for an unpleasant smell or whiff.

clue.text: Tin opener in opulent English boat

parts.note: a can is a tin

indicators.note: the opener of a word is the letter that starts it, so only the first is taken

parts.note: the first letter
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A tin opener inside a luxurious English vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tin opener' reads as the kitchen gadget; the two words do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A canoe is a light narrow boat paddled by hand.

clue.text: Old fogey swapping first love for wayward feats of bravery

indicators.note: swapping one thing for another replaces it, so a letter is taken out and a word put in its place

parts.note: a dodo is an old-fashioned, out-of-date person
love is zero in tennis scoring, hence O; this is the first one in the word
erring means straying, wayward

explanation.surface: An old bore abandoning a first love for something wilder becomes a daring act.
explanation.definitionFit: Derring-do is heroic, daring action, an old phrase for courageous exploits.

clue.text: Unscrupulous lawyers shot by nuns leaving island

indicators.note: when something leaves, it goes away, so that letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a shy is a throw or shot, as at a coconut shy
nuns are called sisters
I is the abbreviation for island; it is removed

explanation.surface: Crooked lawyers were gunned down by nuns fleeing an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like a past-tense verb, but it is the noun meaning a throw; a coconut shy is a fairground stall where people throw balls at coconuts.
explanation.definitionFit: A shyster is a dishonest lawyer or other professional who uses shady methods.

clue.text: Slave from east held in outskirts of Antioch again

indicators.note: held in means enclosed within, so one piece sits inside the other
the outskirts are the edges, so only the outer letters are used

parts.note: the first and last letters

indicators.note: read from the east means right to left on the page, so the word is turned backwards

parts.note: a serf is a feudal slave

explanation.surface: An escaped slave from the east is detained on the edge of the ancient city of Antioch once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Afresh means anew, starting over, which is to do something again.
